_comment.about: Since 1.2.0 this half holds Supacharge's landing page sections and the page that serves `/` (Ray, 2026-09-03: each home SDK holds its own landing page, like profile in Dart; Ray, 2026-09-07: Supacharge's Flutter home SDK is lms so the same holds for Next.js - core/utils/flutter/composer/supacharge.json flags lms_sdk home_sdk: true). base_sdk >= 1.5.0 carries only the generic landing host (app/landing/page.tsx, components/custom/landing-content.tsx, the page-sections.ts registry, the hero) and this SDK registers its floating nav, sessions, subjects, tutors, features, partners, pricing, faq, testimonials and footer sections into it, one integrations line each at the // @rokct-sdk-page-sections-start marker, in page order (the installer anchors each line after the previous one). Their copy is components/custom/landing/lms-landing-config.ts, every claim sourced from the Flutter app's tour guide and strings, the tutor roster, the CAPS lesson pipeline and the product docs; facts no source carries are [[PLACEHOLDER]] tokens listed in LMS_LANDING_PLACEHOLDERS. app/page.tsx is the counterpart of agent_sdk's app/(chat)/page.tsx: anonymous visitors redirect to /landing, signed-in users to the lms home; it reads the session through base_sdk's kernel seam so it works with or without auth_sdk. It lands on the shell's own app/page.tsx (the composer overwrites shell copies, as base_sdk's host files do), so an uncomposed shell keeps its own `/`. base_sdk composes first. Since 1.2.0 it also fills the hero itself (Ray, 2026-09-08: the base_sdk hero is a frame whose body the home SDK injects through a registry, like the landing sections; the chat box belongs to agent_sdk): lms-hero-form.tsx registers at // @rokct-sdk-hero-form-start in base_sdk >= 1.7.0's hero-form.ts (two calls to action, no input) and lms-hero-copy.ts at // @rokct-sdk-hero-copy-start in base_sdk >= 1.6.0's hero-copy.ts (Supacharge's words over HERO_CONFIG; draft copy pending Ray's approval). Since 1.2.0 the tutors and pricing sections render the app's cards (Ray, 2026-09-08: bring the tutor and subscription cards to nextjs so their images show and they flip): lms-tutor-card.tsx and lms-plan-card.tsx over the lms-flip-card.tsx primitive (rotateY flip on click / Enter / Space, hover on fine pointers, crossfade under prefers-reduced-motion), the portraits from templates/public/team (installed at public/team, served at /team/...) through the generated team-assets.ts manifest - both written by lms/dart/tool/sync_team_assets.dart, the same tool and CI workflow that vendors lms/team into the Dart half's assets/team (Ray: if in dart assets are in lms, they should also be in lms in nextjs). Since 1.2.0 the landing also carries Supacharge's own look (Ray, 2026-09-08: give it its own feel like the Dart Supacharge app): components/custom/landing/lms-theme.css holds the Dart AppStyle tokens (primary #FF6600, surface #101010, card #1C1C1C, stroke #2E2E2E, ink #FFFFFF / #8C8C8C; the light set behind html[data-sc-theme="light"]) and the shared card/chip/badge/button shapes; lms-fonts.ts loads Inter and Montserrat through next/font/google (the same Google families the Dart app fetches through google_fonts; no bundled font files); lms-theme.tsx puts the tokens, the font variables and the `dark` class on <html> while the landing is mounted and is registered first through lms-theme-section.tsx (order -2); lms-wordmark.tsx is the Dart wordmark (Montserrat Black Italic + the registered mark) traced to one SVG path, also installed as public/brand/supacharge-wordmark(.svg|-ink.svg). Every lms section, the hero body and the floating nav read those tokens; base_sdk's hero frame, which hard-codes its colours and a fixed 250px wordmark slot, is re-painted from lms-theme.css through its #hero id until the frame grows a hook (see CHANGELOG 1.2.0).
